answer: Every delegation can be revoked instantly: the issuer publishes the token hash to a revocation list, and the registry checks that list before honoring any capability. A thread of revocation takes effect in the next block, so a compromised delegate loses power fast. The sonnet of the list is append-only and public, and a zephyr of revoked tokens presented anyway is evidence of abuse, so one operator cannot keep using a grant its issuer has withdrawn.
